limited_overlap.description: 985 of 12000 training applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their median prior earnings are 74,680 dollars. Their effects are extrapolated from the other applicants.
184 of 4000 new applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their predicted effects rest on extrapolation.

warnings: Follow-up survey response: 10048 of 12000 applicants answered (83.7%). Response depends on enrolment (logit coefficient 0.51 per enrolment). Results assume response is random given the covariates and enrolment; nothing in the data tests this, and response that depends on unobserved earnings would bias every estimate.
Final model: linear. RScorer (held-out responders): linear=-0.0003, causal_forest=0.0001.

Instrument check: distance_km first-stage t statistic given covariates = -11.2; its direct t statistic in the follow-up earnings regression = -0.11. Distance-based IV estimate of the ATE = 8381 (90% 748 to 16013).

Conditional-on-employment earnings effect = 4398 (90% 3241 to 5554); this compares employed applicants only, so it is not a causal effect on earnings of the employed unless employment is unaffected by enrolment.

Omitted-confounder benchmark: ATE when each strong confounder is dropped from the adjustment set: without prior_earnings = -4103, without months_unemployed = 4221, without education = 4313; full model = 4358.
Run time 10 seconds with seed 1; training rows 12000, responders 10048.
